summary: The buy now, pay later company may start a U.S. earned wage access service as an “income-smoothing” complement to its business.
content: Buy now, pay later provider Zip is exploring a potential expansion into earned wage access in the United States. The proposed service is intended to act as an income-smoothing complement to the company's existing financial operations, offering users a new tool to manage their cash flow.

UK Payments Infrastructure Faces a New Test: Preparing for AI-Driven Payments
summary:
The UK has an opportunity to design its next generation of retail payments infrastructure for an economy where money increasingly moves in real time and around the clock. That means looking beyond how quickly a payment can be initiated and considering whether the infrastructure behind it can support real-time settlement, liquidity and reconciliation as well.
Many payment systems today are only partially real time, combining an instant customer experience with legacy processes behind the scenes. As transaction volumes grow and new payment models emerge, that disconnect will become increasingly difficult to sustain.
The priority should be building a modernisation foundation that gives the UK flexibility to support account-to-account payments, cross-border transactions and emerging forms of digital money without having to redesign the underlying infrastructure for each new use case. At the same time, greater speed cannot come at the expense of resilience. In an always-on payments environment, the infrastructure supporting transactions needs to be just as available, secure and resilient as the services customers see.
The biggest risk is treating these as separate challenges. Infrastructure designed too narrowly for today's payment models will need to be patched as new use cases emerge, and patching creates fragmentation. Fragmentation, in turn, undermines resilience, because complexity is the enemy of availability in an always-on environment. The UK should be most concerned about locking in an architecture that looks modern at launch but cannot evolve without being rebuilt.
For the next generation infrastructure to deliver on that, the final framework needs to set out a clear commitment to real-time gross settlement as the foundation of what comes next. Equally important is interoperability: between domestic payment rails, cross-border systems and emerging forms of digital money. That needs to be designed in from the start, not retrofitted. The UK has a genuine opportunity to make infrastructure choices now that will determine its flexibility for the next decade, and the final report should reflect that ambition.
#PaymentsInfrastructureKanv Pandit, Head of International Markets – Banking and PaymentsHead of International Markets – Fidelity Information Services (FIS)10 Sep, 2026
content: The UK must modernise its retail payments infrastructure to prepare for real-time, AI-driven transactions. Experts warn that combining instant customer experiences with legacy back-end processes creates unsustainable fragmentation and risks resilience. The next-generation framework requires real-time gross settlement, built-in interoperability, and the flexibility to support account-to-account payments, cross-border transfers, and digital money without requiring constant rebuilding.
content_ta: ரியல்-டைம் மற்றும் AI-அடிப்படையிலான பரிவர்த்தனைகளுக்கு தயாராகும் வகையில் UK தனது சில்லறை கட்டண உள்கட்டமைப்பை நவீனமயமாக்க வேண்டும். உடனடி வாடிக்கையாளர் அனுபவங்களை பழமையான பின்னணி செயல்முறைகளுடன் இணைப்பது முரண்பாடுகளை உருவாக்குவதாகவும், அதன் ஸ்திரத்தன்மைக்கு ஆபத்தாக முடியும் என்றும் நிபுணர்கள் எச்சரிக்கின்றனர். அடுத்த தலைமுறை கட்டமைப்புக்கு ரியல்-டைம் கிராஸ் செட்டில்மென்ட், ஒருங்கிணைந்த இயங்குதன்மை மற்றும் தொடர்ந்து மறுவடிவமைப்பு செய்யத் தேவையின்றி கணக்குடைய பரிமாற்றங்கள், எல்லை தாண்டிய பரிவர்த்தனைகள் மற்றும் டிஜிட்டல் பணத்தை ஆதரிக்கும் நெகிழ்வுத்தன்மை அவசியமாகும்.
